chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about the missing person, so he said:

The missing person, when four years have passed for him, the ruler sends or writes to the region in which he is absent. If no trace is found for him, the ruler orders his guardian to spend upon her. Whatever he spends upon her, she is his wife.

I said, 'Suppose she says, 'I want what the women want.' He said: 'That is not for her, nor is it honorable. If his guardian or his representative does not spend upon her, he is ordered to divorce her, and that becomes an obligatory divorce for her.'

key_terms.الْمَفْقُودُ: The missing person (one whose whereabouts are unknown)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling for a missing husband after four years?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the procedural framework for determining the marital status of a 'missing person' (mafqud) after a four-year period of absence, emphasizing the ruler's (wali) role in investigation and financial maintenance. It clarifies that the wife's status remains intact until the guardian formally initiates divorce, which becomes obligatory if maintenance ceases, thereby preventing indefinite limbo in family law. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on administrative justice and the protection of women's rights in the absence of the husband.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said about the lost one. So he<sup>asws</sup> said:

‘The lost one, where there pass by four years for him, the ruler should write to the area in which he disappeared in. So if no trace is found for him, the ruler would order his guardian that he should spend upon her. So whatever he spends upon her, she is his wife’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘I said, ‘Suppose she is saying, ‘I want what the women want’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘That is not for her, nor is it honourable. So if his guardian or his representative does not spend upon her, he would be instructed to divorce her, so that would be an Obligatory divorce for her’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘ Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “Once abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was asked about the case of a man who is absent and missing. He (the Imam) said, ‘If one is absent and missing for four years the authorities must send in writing to the area where he has disappeared, and if no trace of him is found the authority then commands his guardian to provide maintenance for her and she is his woman.
5 I (the narrator) then said, ‘She may say, “I want what women want.

’” He (the Imam) said, ‘She cannot do so and it is not honorable. If his guardian did not provide maintenance or his attorney, then he (the authority) commands to divorce her and it then is obligatory divorce for her.’”
